anna: hey eng-security — DSAR from an EU (FR) user: full account erasure + certified deletion proof. Legal needs a cert by EOD CET. filing id: 2026-03-19-PRV-412. Heads-up: infra flagged a vuln (priv esc PoC) and forensics wants a short hold to snapshot. Need clear next steps: retention exception process + KMS/key rotation implications. @mike @sam

mike: ack. do we know if PII is in embeddings/backups? backups complicate deletion chain.

anna: yes — embeddings + S3 snapshots in eu-west-1. no third-party shares.

sam: forensics: hold looks short. we can snapshot EBS + S3 and tag resources with `legal_hold=true`. BUT KMS rotation could affect ability to prove decryption later. @kms-bot pls confirm rotation window.

kms-bot: KMS key alias `redwood/eu-prod-embed`. next scheduled automatic rotation: 2026-03-21T02:00:00Z. rotation only creates a new key version; old key material remains usable for decryption unless the CMK is scheduled for deletion or disabled. schedule-deletion must be prevented while proof is needed.

mike: ok plan draft: 1) file a retention_exception in the privacy system 2) tag snapshots + set `legal_hold=true` 3) prevent any key deletion / ensure key policy allows decryption for archived snapshots 4) export CloudTrail/audit logs proving snapshot + tagging + approvals. who can run the audit export?

sam: I can run CloudTrail export and drop artifacts in vault. example commands I will use:
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:s3:::redwood-embeds-eu --start-time '2026-03-19T00:00:00Z' --end-time '2026-03-20T00:00:00Z'
```
and tagging: 
```
aws s3api put-object-tagging --bucket redwood-embeds-eu --key snaps/2026-03-19.tar.gz --tagging 'TagSet=[{Key=legal_hold,Value=true}]'
```
I will place artifacts at `s3://redwood-legal/forensics/2026-03-19-PRV-412/` and post a signed digest.

lisa: legal needs the following in the final cert: object hashes (sha256), exact deletion timestamp, key id(s) used to encrypt objects, copy of audit logs that show who approved the retention_exception, and the retention_exception ticket id.

anna: quick Q — can we produce an interim "preservation certificate" while hold is active? forensics?

forensics-bot: we will not delete while investigating. we can produce a capture artifact: snapshot hash + signed statement that we captured pre-delete state and are holding it for x hours. that should serve as an interim preservation cert. final deletion cert issued after review completes.

mike: ops actions to take now: create retention_exception ticket and include case id + approvers; create temporary RBAC role `legal_forensics_readonly` (cloudtrail lookup + s3:getobject) restricted to the bucket and time window; annotate KMS key policy to prevent schedule-deletion for 7 days; create `subject_request_lock=true` tagging on subsequent writes to avoid accidental deletes. who will apply RBAC?

sam: I will open infra PR to create the role with an MFA condition and 48h TTL. will also add a key policy patch to block `ScheduleKeyDeletion` for the CMK for 7 days. logging: I'll attach the PR and the IAM policy snippet to the retention ticket.

anna: :thumbsup: filing retention_exception now and cc'ing legal. lisa, what language should go into the ticket for auditors?

lisa: include: case id, justification (forensic hold due to potential vuln), exact resources (bucket ARNs / snapshot ids), retention window length and expiration, approvers (names + slack ts), link to exported audit artifact, and statement that key schedule-deletion is blocked for the window. i'll sign once artifacts are uploaded.

mike: i'll add an automated tracer that tags any writes to embed buckets with `subject_request_lock=true` and alert on attempts to delete.

anna: thanks all. i'll update DSAR tracker and ping if cert timing slips.

sam: will post artifacts and PR links in this thread once ready.

forensics-bot: note: if we later need longer hold, escalation path is legal -> CISO approval.

anna: good to close for now, keeping thread open until artifacts are in the ticket.
